#915

## What to build

Every kit test that copies a prepared scratch (the shared testkit's prepare-once-per-gate-run copy, and any other prepared-repo copy in the testkit or tests/lib) copies a quiescent git repo: no git command a scenario or its kit commands run in a scratch starts git's automatic background maintenance (gc --auto, maintenance --auto, detached), so the copy never races a vanishing `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` or a repacking object store. Seam, agreed before any test: the testkit's Scratch interface (its environment, `run`, `git` and `prepare`), the one shared world every kit test goes through (testkit docstring); a new kit test drives that interface and shows auto-maintenance is not started in a scratch repo even when the repo's own config would trigger it at once, and the same test fails on the code before the fix. Tests only, smallest change, no product change, no retry or ignore-on-copy workaround in place of quiescence.

Demo: `just test tests/gate/kit/test_template_languages.py::test_claims_gate tests/gate/kit/test_qc_one_execution.py` runs the two items that hit the race on main and on PR #823 CI, green; the new race test is its own gate item.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] rule: kit tests are deterministic under load, a prepared scratch copy never races git background maintenance (owner ruling #915)
- [ ] the new kit test fails on main before the fix (git starts auto maintenance in a scratch repo) and passes after it
- [ ] every prepared-repo copy in the testkit and tests/lib audited; each that copies a git repo is covered by the same fix or named as not affected
- [ ] demo: `just test tests/gate/kit/test_template_languages.py::test_claims_gate tests/gate/kit/test_qc_one_execution.py` passes

## What to build

The qc sandbox's live-survivor kit test reads its survivor's pid only once the stand-in bwrap has written it whole: the stand-in publishes the pidfile atomically (written beside it, then renamed into place), so the test never reads an empty or partial pidfile while the survivor is still writing it (seen on lane CI as `int('')` at the pidfile read). Tests only, smallest change, no product change, no retry loop in place of an atomic publish. Proof the old shape races: with the window between the pidfile's create and its write widened, the old stand-in makes the test read an empty file and fail; the new one passes.
